laws.rule: Osaka Prefecture's accommodation tax, from stays on 1 September 2025: none under JPY 5,000 a person a night; JPY 200 from JPY 5,000 to 14,999; JPY 400 from JPY 15,000 to 19,999; JPY 500 from JPY 20,000 (about A$4.51, RBA rate of 30 October 2026).
laws.heading: 大阪府の宿泊税

laws.rule: Since 27 January 2025 Osaka City bans smoking, including heated tobacco, on all city-managed roads, squares, parks and other public places across the whole city. Smoking there brings a JPY 1,000 penalty (about A$9.02, RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82). Use designated smoking areas.
laws.heading: 大阪市路上喫煙の防止に関する条例 (amended)

laws.rule: Osaka Prefecture's 大阪府青少年健全育成条例 (Osaka Youth Healthy Development Ordinance), art. 25 and 41. The night hours depend on age: 8 pm to 4 am for under 16, 11 pm to 4 am for 16 and 17. A guardian must try not to let a young person out in those hours without good reason (commute to work or school, for example). Anyone else, including by phone or message calls, is barred from taking the young person out, going about with them or keeping them out in those hours without the guardian's consent. The offence carries a fine of up to JPY 300,000 (about A$2,707). Rates: RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82.
laws.heading: 大阪府青少年健全育成条例 (Osaka), curfew for young people

laws.rule: Osaka City, Kita and Minami entertainment districts (Minami covers the Dotonbori and Shinsaibashi area; the city's zone map is linked on its page): 大阪市客引き行為等の適正化に関する条例 (Osaka Touting Ordinance) bans touting, soliciting a particular person to use a service, and waiting to do so, in designated "prohibited zones", in any trade, and having others do it (art. 10). The mayor can guide, warn, then order the person to stop (art. 11); breaking an order is punishable by an administrative fine (過料) of up to JPY 50,000 (about A$451, RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82) (art. 16). Since 1 April 2021 a repeat offender goes straight to an order. It binds touts and shop owners, not people who are approached. Article text is from the city's 2017 consolidated copy; the city's current page was read for the zones and the fine.

Osaka City asks people not to dive into the Dotonbori River from Ebisu Bridge, other bridges or the riverside walks, and not to jump up and down on bridges. The city's notice of 15 October 2026 says the water near Ebisu Bridge is about 3.5 metres deep, the water falls below 10 degrees C in winter, boats use the river, and past dives have caused deaths and injuries. The notice is a request; it names no ordinance or fine.
